reasoning: Recent Alaska Senate polling is very tight: one early-August poll shows Mary Peltola ahead of Dan Sullivan by 1.6 points in the final ranked-choice round, while another late-July/early-August poll shows Sullivan ahead by 2 points in the initial round. No current Alaska presidential head-to-head poll from the last 45 days surfaced, so the best current race read is that the Senate contest is effectively even with a slight Democratic edge within polling error.

sources.name: Alaska Survey Research
sources.details: Final-round ranked-choice result showed Mary Peltola 50.8% and Dan Sullivan 49.2% among likely Alaska general-election voters.

sources.name: Data for Progress
sources.details: Survey of likely Alaska voters found Peltola leading Sullivan 47% to 41% in the first round of ranked-choice voting.

sources.name: The New York Times/Siena University
sources.details: New York Times/Siena poll found Sullivan ahead of Peltola 47% to 45% in the initial round of ranked-choice voting.

sources.name: Cook Political Report Cook PVI
sources.details: Cook Political Report's statewide Alaska PVI is R+9, indicating a solid Republican lean in presidential vote history.
